title: A torch and a sheet of paper for the angle test (home guide on the portal)
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y6 lesson 6 (A torch and a sheet of paper for the angle test (home guide on the portal))
intro: Lesson 6: Polar climate: cold, dark and dry. To understand why the polar regions are so cold and have long days and nights

questions.q: Why does slanted sunlight warm the ground less?
questions.a: Its energy is spread over a bigger area
questions.model: Torch straight down: small bright circle. Torch slanted: big dim patch. Same energy, bigger area, so less warming.

questions.q: What was the coldest temperature recorded at Vostok?

questions.a: When the sun does not rise for 24 hours or more

questions.q: Core: Write a polar climate fact box with four facts (temperature, rain or snow, day and night, wind).
questions.a: For example: down to -89.2 °C; very little snow; polar day and night; strong winds
questions.model: Teacher shows fact 1: 'Temperature: Antarctica can reach -89.2 °C, the coldest ever recorded.'

questions.q: Extend: Explain why the poles are cold, using the torch idea.
questions.a: Sunlight arrives at a low angle, so its energy is spread out; ice also reflects sunlight

questions.q: Stretch: How do Muslims living far north work out prayer times in summer when it hardly gets dark?
questions.a: Scholars give rulings to estimate times, for example by following the times of a nearer place or a fixed pattern

questions.q: Big question: how do people pray when the sun does not set for weeks?
questions.a: Scholars advise estimating prayer times, for example from a nearby place, as the Prophet taught for days of unusual length
